captions.instagram:
How does a drone fly?

A drone has no tilting blades and no gearbox, yet it hovers, climbs and turns on the spot. It does it by changing four propellers' speeds up to hundreds of times a second.

→ A quadcopter has four motors, four propellers, a flight controller, a battery and a GPS.
→ A gust tips the drone. Its controller senses the tilt and speeds two motors up or down to push back.
→ Too much proportional gain makes it overshoot and wobble, because nothing damps the swing.
→ To move forward, a quadcopter tips: the thrust leans, and the drone goes where it points.
→ To turn, two diagonal rotors speed up while the other pair slows, so their twists no longer cancel.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/droneclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a drone fly? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A drone has no tilting blades and no gearbox, yet it hovers, climbs and turns on the spot. It does it by changing four propellers' speeds up to hundreds of times a second.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/droneclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/droneclear

In this video:
• The one-line idea. A quadcopter moves by changing how fast four propellers spin.
• The part people get wrong. A drone does not stay level by magic.
• Keeping level. The P, I and D dials set how hard, how long and how smoothly the drone corrects.
• Moving. Lean to fly forward, speed all four to climb, and speed one diagonal pair to turn.
• The battery. Watt-hours against hover power set the flight time, and every extra gram of payload costs minutes.
• The rules and the uses. India's Drone Rules, 2021 set green, yellow and red airspace and register drones on Digital Sky.
